ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Three unit circles, each with radius 1 meter, lie in the same plane such that the center of each circle is one intersection point between the two other circles, as shown below. Mass is uniformly distributed among all area enclosed by at least one circle. The mass of the region enclosed by the triangle shown above is $1 \mathrm{~kg}$. Let $x$ be the moment of inertia of the area enclosed by all three circles (intersection, not union) about the axis perpendicular to the page and through the center of mass of the triangle. Then, $x$ can be expressed as $\frac{a \pi-b \sqrt{c}}{d \sqrt{e}}$ $\mathrm{kg} \mathrm{m}^{2}$, where $a, b, c, d, e$ are integers such that $\operatorname{gcd}(a, b, d)=1$ and both $c$ and $e$ are squarefree. Compute $a+b+c+d+e$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: In the image, three unit circles of different colors can be seen overlapping each other: the red circle is above, the blue circle is at the lower left, and the green circle is at the lower right. The three vertices of the black triangle are exactly the centers of the three circles, and at the same time are the intersection points of the other two circles. Therefore the black triangle is an equilateral triangle with side length 1, and its centroid is denoted as O. The area of the triangle is sqrt(3)/4, and the problem gives that the mass of this triangular region is 1 kg, so the surface density is rho = 1/(sqrt(3)/4) = 4/sqrt(3). The common intersection of the three circles is the Reuleaux triangle region around the black triangle. It can be decomposed into the sum of three sectors with radius 1 and central angle 60°, then subtracting twice the central equilateral triangle, because when the three sectors are added, the central triangle has been counted repeatedly three times. For a 60° unit sector: the area A = pi/6; the polar second moment about its own circle center is pi/12; the distance from the centroid of this sector to the circle center is 2/pi, in the direction along the angle bisector; the distance from the circle center to O is 1/sqrt(3). Therefore using the parallel-axis/translation formula, the geometric polar second moment of a single sector about O is J_sector,O = pi/12 + (pi/6)(1/3) - 2/(3sqrt(3)) = 5pi/36 - 2/(3sqrt(3)). The geometric polar second moment of an equilateral triangle with side length 1 about its centroid O is J_triangle,O = sqrt(3)/48. Therefore the geometric polar second moment of the common intersection region is J = 3J_sector,O - 2J_triangle,O = 3(5pi/36 - 2/(3sqrt(3))) - 2(sqrt(3)/48) = (10pi - 17sqrt(3))/24. Multiplying by the surface density gives the moment of inertia x = rho J = (4/sqrt(3)) * (10pi - 17sqrt(3))/24 = (10pi - 17sqrt(3))/(6sqrt(3)) kg m^2. So a=10, b=17, c=3, d=6, e=3, hence a+b+c+d+e = 10+17+3+6+3 = 39.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the three colored circles form a threefold-symmetric common intersection, with the black equilateral triangle joining their centers. Put the centroid O of the black triangle at the origin, and place the three circle centers at distance R = 1/sqrt(3) from O. The triangle side length is 1, so its area is sqrt(3)/4 and the density is rho = 4/sqrt(3). Instead of decomposing into sectors, integrate the polar second moment of the common intersection directly. By the threefold symmetry seen in the image, it is enough to integrate over one 120-degree wedge whose boundary is one circular arc, then multiply by 3. In that wedge, measure angle theta from the ray pointing from O away from the opposite circle center, with -pi/3 <= theta <= pi/3. The active boundary is the unit circle centered a distance R in the opposite direction, so the radial boundary satisfies r^2 + 2Rr cos(theta) + R^2 = 1, hence r_max(theta) = -R cos(theta) + sqrt(1 - R^2 sin^2(theta)). Therefore the geometric polar moment is J = 3 * integral_{-pi/3}^{pi/3} integral_0^{r_max(theta)} r^3 dr dtheta = (3/4) integral_{-pi/3}^{pi/3} r_max(theta)^4 dtheta. Evaluating this exact trigonometric integral with R=1/sqrt(3) gives J = (10pi - 17sqrt(3))/24. Multiplying by rho gives x = (10pi - 17sqrt(3))/(6sqrt(3)), yielding a+b+c+d+e = 10+17+3+6+3 = 39.

先描述图像：图中有三个同半径圆，分别用红、蓝、绿表示；它们呈三重对称排列。黑色线段连接三个圆心，形成一个等边三角形。每个圆心都位于另外两个圆的交点处，三圆的公共交集是中间的三重对称曲边区域。

再推理：设黑色等边三角形的质心为 O，并把 O 作为原点。三个圆心就是等边三角形的三个顶点。因为圆半径为 1，且每个圆心在另外两个圆上，所以三角形边长为 1。等边三角形面积为 sqrt(3)/4。题目给出该三角形区域质量为 1 kg，且面密度均匀，所以面密度 rho = 1 / (sqrt(3)/4) = 4/sqrt(3)。

等边三角形外接圆半径，即从 O 到每个圆心的距离为 R = 1/sqrt(3)。要求的是三圆公共交集关于过 O 且垂直纸面的轴的转动惯量。先求几何极惯量 J = ∬ r^2 dA，再乘以 rho。

由图中的三重对称性，只需取一个 120 度楔形区域，再乘以 3。令角度 theta 从 O 指向远离相对圆心的射线开始计，范围为 -pi/3 <= theta <= pi/3。该楔形中的有效边界来自圆心在相反方向、距 O 为 R 的单位圆。其极坐标边界满足 r^2 + 2Rr cos(theta) + R^2 = 1，因此 r_max(theta) = -R cos(theta) + sqrt(1 - R^2 sin^2(theta))。

所以公共交集的几何极惯量为 J = 3 * ∫_{-pi/3}^{pi/3} ∫_0^{r_max(theta)} r^3 dr dtheta = (3/4) ∫_{-pi/3}^{pi/3} r_max(theta)^4 dtheta。代入 R = 1/sqrt(3) 并精确计算该积分，得到 J = (10pi - 17sqrt(3))/24。

于是质量转动惯量 x = rho J = (4/sqrt(3)) * (10pi - 17sqrt(3))/24 = (10pi - 17sqrt(3))/(6sqrt(3)) kg m^2。与形式 (a pi - b sqrt(c))/(d sqrt(e)) 对比，可取 a=10, b=17, c=3, d=6, e=3。于是 a+b+c+d+e = 10+17+3+6+3 = 39。

先描述图像：图中有三个同半径圆，分别用红、蓝、绿表示；它们呈三重对称排列。黑色线段连接三个圆心，形成一个等边三角形。每个圆心都位于另外两个圆的交点处，三圆的公共交集是中间的三重对称曲边区域。

再推理：设黑色等边三角形的质心为 O，并把 O 作为原点。三个圆心就是等边三角形的三个顶点。因为圆半径为 1，且每个圆心在另外两个圆上，所以三角形边长为 1。等边三角形面积为 sqrt(3)/4。题目给出该三角形区域质量为 1 kg，且面密度均匀，所以面密度 rho = 1 / (sqrt(3)/4) = 4/sqrt(3)。

等边三角形外接圆半径，即从 O 到每个圆心的距离为 R = 1/sqrt(3)。要求的是三圆公共交集关于过 O 且垂直纸面的轴的转动惯量。先求几何极惯量 J = ∬ r^2 dA，再乘以 rho。

由图中的三重对称性，只需取一个 120 度楔形区域，再乘以 3。令角度 theta 从 O 指向远离相对圆心的射线开始计，范围为 -pi/3 <= theta <= pi/3。该楔形中的有效边界来自圆心在相反方向、距 O 为 R 的单位圆。其极坐标边界满足 r^2 + 2Rr cos(theta) + R^2 = 1，因此 r_max(theta) = -R cos(theta) + sqrt(1 - R^2 sin^2(theta))。

所以公共交集的几何极惯量为 J = 3 * ∫_{-pi/3}^{pi/3} ∫_0^{r_max(theta)} r^3 dr dtheta = (3/4) ∫_{-pi/3}^{pi/3} r_max(theta)^4 dtheta。代入 R = 1/sqrt(3) 并精确计算该积分，得到 J = (10pi - 17sqrt(3))/24。

于是质量转动惯量 x = rho J = (4/sqrt(3)) * (10pi - 17sqrt(3))/24 = (10pi - 17sqrt(3))/(6sqrt(3)) kg m^2。与形式 (a pi - b sqrt(c))/(d sqrt(e)) 对比，可取 a=10, b=17, c=3, d=6, e=3。于是 a+b+c+d+e = 10+17+3+6+3 = 39。

raw_record.original_question: Three unit circles, each with radius 1 meter, lie in the same plane such that the center of each circle is one intersection point between the two other circles, as shown below. Mass is uniformly distributed among all area enclosed by at least one circle. The mass of the region enclosed by the triangle shown above is $1 \mathrm{~kg}$. Let $x$ be the moment of inertia of the area enclosed by all three circles (intersection, not union) about the axis perpendicular to the page and through the center of mass of the triangle. Then, $x$ can be expressed as $\frac{a \pi-b \sqrt{c}}{d \sqrt{e}}$ $\mathrm{kg} \mathrm{m}^{2}$, where $a, b, c, d, e$ are integers such that $\operatorname{gcd}(a, b, d)=1$ and both $c$ and $e$ are squarefree. Compute $a+b+c+d+e$.
raw_record.final_cot:
In the image, three unit circles of different colors can be seen overlapping each other: the red circle is above, the blue circle is at the lower left, and the green circle is at the lower right. The three vertices of the black triangle are exactly the centers of the three circles, and at the same time are the intersection points of the other two circles. Therefore the black triangle is an equilateral triangle with side length 1, and its centroid is denoted as O.

The area of the triangle is sqrt(3)/4, and the problem gives that the mass of this triangular region is 1 kg, so the surface density is rho = 1/(sqrt(3)/4) = 4/sqrt(3).

The common intersection of the three circles is the Reuleaux triangle region around the black triangle. It can be decomposed into the sum of three sectors with radius 1 and central angle 60°, then subtracting twice the central equilateral triangle, because when the three sectors are added, the central triangle has been counted repeatedly three times.

For a 60° unit sector: the area A = pi/6; the polar second moment about its own circle center is pi/12; the distance from the centroid of this sector to the circle center is 2/pi, in the direction along the angle bisector; the distance from the circle center to O is 1/sqrt(3). Therefore using the parallel-axis/translation formula, the geometric polar second moment of a single sector about O is J_sector,O = pi/12 + (pi/6)(1/3) - 2/(3sqrt(3)) = 5pi/36 - 2/(3sqrt(3)).

The geometric polar second moment of an equilateral triangle with side length 1 about its centroid O is J_triangle,O = sqrt(3)/48.

Therefore the geometric polar second moment of the common intersection region is J = 3J_sector,O - 2J_triangle,O = 3(5pi/36 - 2/(3sqrt(3))) - 2(sqrt(3)/48) = (10pi - 17sqrt(3))/24.

Multiplying by the surface density gives the moment of inertia x = rho J = (4/sqrt(3)) * (10pi - 17sqrt(3))/24 = (10pi - 17sqrt(3))/(6sqrt(3)) kg m^2.

So a=10, b=17, c=3, d=6, e=3, hence a+b+c+d+e = 10+17+3+6+3 = 39.
